name: Capsule generation and single-copy barcoding module v1
description: One 150 x 100 mm board carrying the three stages that replace the bought capsule generator and the plate-based barcoding rounds of a published single-cell chromatin workflow. Stage A (y ~78) makes core-shell capsules: shell and core streams each pass a guard filter, meet at nozzle_1, and are cut into droplets by oil; delay_1 is a dark residence line, and capsules are collected and cured off-chip because the aqueous two-phase core-shell has to demix first, which takes minutes rather than the ~20 s a sensible on-chip serpentine can hold. Stage B (y ~50) is the new part: capsules are re-injected close-packed through pack_1, meet one aqueous stream carrying the amplification mix and a single-copy barcode, and are cut back into oil at nozzle_2, so each capsule ends up alone in a droplet with its own barcode. Stage C (y ~20) replaces about twenty centrifugation steps: brk_1 separates oil from the aqueous phase, trap_1 holds the capsules as a packed bed while buffers flow past, and the bed is back-flushed out of out_recover. EVERY FEATURE IS >= 100 um, so the whole board is embossed in one step from a single 0.15 mm deep cavity layer; there is no photolithography anywhere. Capsules are 120-150 um, deliberately larger than the ~70 um of the published workflow, because close-packed re-injection needs an entrance of about 0.85 x capsule diameter and 0.85 x 70 um = 60 um is below what we can make. Geometry and flow numbers are ours; the biology they serve is cited in protocols/sctip_spc_v1.json.

chambers.note: Guard filter only: 150 um pillars on a 250 um pitch, 100 um gaps, 3 staggered rows. It stops gel lumps reaching a 100 um orifice. It CANNOT strain cell clumps, because a 100 um gap passes a clump of five cells; cells are strained off-chip at 40 um.
Same guard filter on the core line, which carries the permeabilised cells.

Flow-focusing cross. Orifice 100 um wide x 150 um deep x 150 um long, the smallest feature on the board. Chosen over step emulsification because a step terrace for this droplet size would be ~45 um deep and would clog on cells.
Dark residence line. NOT a cure window: see the chip description.

Close-packed re-injection entrance, 115 um wide against a 135 um capsule (0.85 x d). This ratio is what beats Poisson on the capsule: published work gets 93-97% single occupancy this way. It is also the reason the capsules are 135 um and not 70 um.
Second flow-focusing cross, 150 um orifice, cuts one capsule plus its barcode back into oil.

Phase separation. A row of 100 x 150 um slots on a 300 um pitch, wetted for the aqueous phase; oil leaves through the separate hydrophobic line to out_oil. This is the step the bench protocol loses the most capsules at, so it is the main thing the chip is for.

Packed-bed trap replacing ~20 centrifugation steps. Retention is by chamber geometry and gravity with downward flow, NOT by a size gap: a liquid-core capsule deforms, and the gap that would reliably hold a 135 um capsule is ~0.5-0.6 x d = 70-80 um, which we cannot make. Buffer exchange is diffusion-limited at ~2-5 min, not flush-limited.

ports.note: one capsule per droplet, to the thermocycler
thermocycled emulsion back from the tube
